prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "image", with the standing line "Turns a finished prompt into a saved picture file, with each paid API call recorded in a ledger." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows Two paper sheets, the technical prompt and the enhanced prompt, slide together into one joined sheet. The sheet drops through a key-shaped gate for the API key check, then through a second gate, a registry drawer that admits only listed OpenAI image models, with gpt-image-2 marked as the default. The sheet leaves rightward as an outgoing request, and a response returns along a parallel arrow. At the point of return, a ledger book receives one entry. Picture bytes then fall downward into a folder named generated as a .png file. From there a thin caption strip is fixed along the bottom of the picture, and the path continues toward .

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows the key gate open onto nothing: an empty .png placeholder, with no request sent. The second circle shows the registry drawer refusing an old model card before any payment. The third circle shows the ledger book close up, one row per response. The studies are three frames, square, wide, and tall, each chosen by a word found in the prompt.

Colour is used so that Amber marks the paid request and the ledger. Brick red marks refusal paths. Slate blue marks files written to disk.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 2 prompt sheets joined into 1 request. 3 frame shapes: square, wide, tall. 1 ledger row per API response. 1 attempt, with no retries. 3 progress phases along the foot. 2 output folders: generated and annotated.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: technical prompt and enhanced prompt on the two incoming sheets. gpt-image-2 on the registry drawer's default card. image ledger on the book at the response return. generated on the first folder holding the .png file. annotated on the final folder. terse prompt on the caption strip. image_wait on the timeline while the request is out. image_download on the timeline once bytes arrive. annotate on the timeline where the caption is added. landscape and vertical on the frames that those prompt words select.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: technical prompt, enhanced prompt, joined prompt, API key check, model registry, gpt-image-2, image request, response, generated, .png, caption added missing key, empty placeholder, unsupported model, refused before paying, image ledger square, landscape, vertical, quality high annotated, terse prompt caption, opened locally image_wait, image_download, annotate

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Two prompts joined into one request; Size chosen from words in prompt No key: empty file, no API call; Legacy models refused before a paid request; One ledger row per API response Terse prompt lettered along the bottom Phase changes when download begins; Single attempt, no retries
